chunks: He said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn reported to me, from his father, who reported from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, who reported from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Sahban, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family, said:
"Blessed is he who leaves a present desire for a promised reward he has not seen."

key_terms.شهوة: Shahwa - desire, craving, lust; refers to worldly temptations
key_terms.طوبى: Tuba - blessedness, paradise, or a tree in paradise; denotes supreme felicity
key_terms.موعود: Maw'ud - that which is promised; refers to divine promises of reward in the hereafter

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Muhammad say about leaving worldly desires for divine promises?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), narrated through Imam al-Sadiq (AS), extols the virtue of self-restraint and delayed gratification in the pursuit of divine promises. This teaching was delivered to encourage believers to forgo immediate worldly pleasures in favor of the unseen rewards of the hereafter, reflecting a central theme in Islamic ethics about trust in God's promises and the superiority of spiritual rewards over temporal pleasures.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 11. He said: Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn reported to me from his father, who reported from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, who reported from Muhammad ibn Abu Al-Sahban, from Muhammad ibn Abu Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, that: Abu Abdillah Ja’far ibn Muhammad (as) who said: The Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, said:
"Blessed is he who denounces the tempting ready desire, to earn the promised blessing he has not seen."
